title: Hardware-Enforced Stack Protection (CET) User Shadow Stacks Disabled
description: Control-flow Enforcement Technology (CET) leverages CPU hardware capabilities (Intel Tiger Lake+, AMD Zen 3+) to maintain a protected shadow stack, preventing ROP (Return-Oriented Programming) exploits.
impact: Memory corruption exploits can redirect call flows and execute arbitrary shellcode in userspace memory.
remediation_guidance: Enable Hardware-Enforced Stack Protection via Windows Security > Exploit Protection or Group Policy.

compliance_mappings.title: Configure Exploit Protection Hardware Shadow Stacks

title: Arbitrary Code Guard (ACG) & Strict Exploit Mitigations Unenforced
description: Arbitrary Code Guard (ACG) prevents dynamic code generation and prohibits modification of executable memory pages (W^X violation prevention).
impact: Injected code can execute arbitrary dynamic payloads within trusted processes.
remediation_guidance: Enforce Arbitrary Code Guard (ACG) system-wide or per-application in Exploit Protection settings.
